summary:
Wrapped up the existing PIXELBOUND: LOST SIGNAL project without starting new features or refactors.

What I did this session:
- Audited the codebase: index.html, styles.css, and all 17 modules under src/ (main, game, input, audio, save, math, tiles, player, level, entities, levelmanager, camera, particles, sprites, render, ui, levels).
- Looked specifically for broken behaviour. Found none: the service handoff reported clean state and my review confirmed the movement feel systems (coyote time 0.11s, jump buffer 0.13s, apex gravity relief, fall-gravity multiplier, variable jump cut, dash with cooldown), the axis-separated swept AABB collision model, one-way/moving/falling/phase platforms, bounce pads, hazards, enemies, checkpoint/integrity respawn flow, save semantics, and menu wiring (settings actually write through to audio gains, camera shake, reduced motion, particles) are all coherent and correctly connected. No "fake" functionality found, so I deliberately made no code edits.
- Wrote README.md: how to play, full keyboard/touch/gamepad controls, movement-feel systems, health + Signal Integrity + respawn rules, collectibles, enemy types, hazards and platform types, the three levels, menus/HUD, save behaviour, accessibility options, and technical notes (fixed 1/60s step, 480x270 logical resolution at 2x, procedural art and audio).
- Wrote REPORT.md: file-by-file architecture and the reasoning behind the splits, per-frame data flow, fixed-timestep rationale, the collision model, a table of tuned game-feel constants with justifications, the documented level-authoring jump budget plus the "lay ground before carving pits" rule, audio synthesis design, save system, responsiveness/mobile/performance work, an honest known-limitations section, and prioritised next steps.

Verification (final, both clean):
- check_project: OK — 17 JS files parse as ES modules, all relative imports/script/src/link targets resolve.
- smoke_test: ok:true — zero uncaught exceptions, zero conso
